transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Triton CTO), Priya Shah (Triton ML Eng), Ken Adams (Triton Product)

Auto-summary:
Triton Freight is planning a 6-week pilot to validate Redwood for routing/assistant features in their freight ops product. Key focus: throughput at peak (50-100 concurrent users), p95 latency targets for short chat flows, end-to-end function/tool calling for manifest lookups, and structured JSON output for downstream systems. Pilot will include Dedicated capacity benchmark runs and an interoperability adapter that maps Triton's event schema to Redwood OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Security and KMS/HSM requirements were flagged as gating items.

Topics covered:
- Workload sizing & concurrency (50-100 concurrent sessions, 15k tokens/day estimate)
- Benchmarks to run: short chat (<=256 tokens), long context (context window 8k), embeddings batch throughput
- Integration choices: Redwood SDK vs native OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- Function/tool calling: manifest lookup, pricing API, shipment status webhooks
- Structured output: strict JSON schema for downstream systems (order, eta_estimates, confidence)
- Timeline: 6-8 week pilot recommended
- Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC peering, audit logs

Action items (recap in call):
- See metadata action_items list above for owners/dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Elena (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for being here, um let's do quick intros and then we'll jump into scope. Marcus and I will drive benchmarks and the SDK integration plan.
[00:18] Ravi (Triton CTO): hey — thanks. Ravi here, CTO. Priya and Ken are on to cover ML and product. We're mostly focused on replacing a part of our routing assistant that currently does heuristics.
[00:30] Marcus (Redwood SE): great, thanks. quick question up front — are you expecting to use the Hosted API for the pilot or do you want Dedicated right away? both options are doable but the benchmark approach changes a bit.
[00:44] Priya (Triton ML Eng): good question. we are leaning Dedicated because our data path touches PII and some regulatory clients ask for isolated capacity. also want predictable latency.
[00:56] Ken (Product Lead): yeah, predictable is huge. We had some spikes in our heuristics service that cause downstream re-routes and SLOs were missed.
[01:08] Elena: okay that helps. for success criteria, can you confirm what matters most — latency p95, throughput, and quality? and any concrete numbers you want to aim for?
[01:20] Ravi: p95 under 350ms for short responses is our target, would be acceptable up to 500ms if quality is significantly better. throughput wise, plan for 50 concurrent agents hitting the model, bursting to 100 at peak. rough token volume is 10-20k tokens per day for pilot, more afterwards.
[01:40] Marcus: noted. we'll run two primary bench scenarios: (1) short chat test with 32-256 tokens per request to measure p95 and tail latencies, (2) long context test with 8k window and KV cache behaviors. plus embeddings throughput for search.
[01:55] Priya: for long context, we have some cases where we append up to 6k tokens of manifest and message history; so KV caching and prefix caching are important — does Redwood support automatic prefix cache eviction?
[02:10] Marcus: yes, the runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache management. exact behavior depends on model and quantization profile; we'll capture that in the benchmark notes.
[02:20] Ken: nuts and bolts — integration. We already have an internal service that expects JSON responses with fields: order_id, eta_minutes, confidence_score. can Redwood guarantee structured output or do we need an adapter?
[02:34] Elena: we support structured output via JSON schema / structured response constraints. there can be some hallucination margin — part of the POC is measuring extraction accuracy. recommended pattern is function/tool calling for lookups + schema enforcement post-model.
[02:50] Ravi: ok show me the tradeoffs — SDK vs OpenAI-compatible endpoints. we have an existing wrapper built around OpenAI SDKs.
[03:02] Marcus: short answer: you can use the OpenAI-compatible endpoints Redwood exposes, which mostly matches your current wrapper with minor header changes. the Redwood SDK gives higher-level helpers for batching, automatic prefix caching, and built-in tool calling wiring which simplifies the adapter work. if you want minimal change, use the OpenAI-compatible route; for better performance and less custom plumbing, the SDK is recommended.
[03:28] Priya: how much engineering effort to swap the current wrapper to the Redwood SDK?
[03:34] Marcus: for basic calls probably 1-2 days. to fully leverage batching, KV cache, and function calling patterns maybe 1-2 sprints (2-4 weeks) of integration work depending on internal reviews.
[03:46] Ken: we prefer minimal lift for pilot, but if the improved perf pays off we'd invest more later.
[03:52] Elena: makes sense. for the pilot we'll propose an adapter approach: keep your existing OpenAI-compatible wrapper but route pilot traffic through a small Redwood SDK proxy that handles batching/caching; that keeps your endpoint shape stable.
[04:08] Ravi: that sounds sensible. benchmarks — what exact metrics will you provide?
[04:14] Marcus: we'll produce: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput (reqs/s and tokens/s), cost per 1M tokens estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated, memory/KV cache hit rates, failure/error rates under load. we'll give CSV/JSON results and a short analysis doc.
[04:36] Priya: and can you test with quantized model variants? we've seen large memory delta between 8-bit and 4-bit in other infra.
[04:44] Marcus: yes we'll include a couple quantization profiles if you want — quantizaiton sometimes affects quality so we'll pair bench runs with a small eval set (your three representative prompts) to check regression.
[04:58] Ravi: about function calling — we need to call our manifest lookup service and then have the model fill a templated response. any examples of recommended pattern?
[05:08] Marcus: recommended pattern is external tool for manifest lookup (tool returns structured dict), then model generates final JSON guided by schema. Redwood supports function/tool calling and has a tooling shim to validate output. we'll share a snippet in the follow-up.
[05:22] Ken: ok — question on network/security — VPC peering + KMS. Is there a way to do a private connector to Redwood Private, or do we need the Dedicated offering with customer-managed VPC?
[05:34] Elena: two options: Redwood Dedicated in a tenant with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, or Redwood Private if you need full on-prem or air-gapped. for the pilot Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS integrations is common and faster to spin up.
[05:50] Ravi: timeline — how long to get Dedicated capacity with peering?
[05:54] Elena: presuming we have PoC SOW approved and security contact, we can provision a Dedicated pool in ~10 business days; VPC peering is normally 2-5 days depending on network approvals. so plan for provisioning week + network work.
[06:08] Priya: can we run a small smoke test on hosted while provisioning Dedicated to avoid idle time?
[06:14] Marcus: absolutely yes — hosted is great for early integration. just note performance will differ from Dedicated; benchmarks will be representative for functional validation only.
[06:26] Ravi: let's talk numbers: what Dedicated sizing do you recommend for our expected peak?
[06:31] Marcus: preliminary suggestion: 4x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent Ampere GPUs) to support 50-100 concurrent short chat sessions with pinned KV cache and modest batch sizes. we'll produce a more exact model after we see your trace.
[06:46] Ken: costs — can you give order-of-magnitude?
[06:49] Elena: we'll send a draft pricing sheet. ballpark: Dedicated commitment for a pilot (3 months) with that sizing will be provided as a committed quote; hosted per-token pricing for initial smoke tests will also be provided.
[07:02] Priya: benchmarks — what test harness do you use? can we run it in our environment to replicate?
[07:08] Marcus: we use a harness that drives OpenAI-style requests with concurrency control, supports variable token sizes, and measures latencies; we can share the harness (open-source-ish) or run the harness from Redwood side against your endpoint. best practice: run both to verify parity.
[07:22] Ravi: we'd like to run them ourselves and get your help.
[07:26] Elena: perfect. Marcus will share the harness and a short how-to.
[07:32] Ken: about structured output, you mentioned schema enforcement — how strict is that? will the model always obey the schema?
[07:40] Marcus: in practice the model follows schema most of the time, but hallucination happens. we recommend a three-step pattern: (1) function/tool for canonical data (2) model generation with schema constraints (3) post-generation validation (a lightweight schema checker). we can automate steps 1/2 with Redwood's tool calling glue.
[08:02] Priya: ok that fits our pipeline. on evals, we need precision recall on entity extraction, and end-to-end test that maps to our KPI of routing accuracy. can Redwood hook into our evaluation harness?
[08:12] Marcus: yes, we'll accept your eval set; we'll run benched prompts and produce per-prompt correctness scores.
[08:20] Ravi: one more security item — audit logs: we need token-level request/response logs retained for 90 days and accessible to our security team. can Redwood do that for Dedicated?
[08:30] Elena: yes, Dedicated includes extended observability and you can opt-in for retention; we have audit logs, tracing hooks, and can integrate with your SIEM via syslog or S3 exports. we'll surface the retention and export mechanics in the security pack.
[08:46] Ken: awesome. any blockers on our side?
[08:49] Priya: we'll need to check with legal on data residency for EU clients, but for pilot it's US-only.
[08:55] Elena: fine. next steps recap: Marcus shares bench matrix, Elena sends SOW and pricing, Ravi will share traces.
[09:03] Ravi: timeline check — ideally pilot kickoff by 2027-09-13, run 4 weeks of active bench + 2 weeks integration review. is that realistic?
[09:12] Marcus: yes that's doable if we get traces and network early. provisioning Dedicated could take that first week but we can do hosted smoke tests before Dedicated is ready.
[09:24] Ken: ok let's aim for that.
[09:28] Elena: i'll include a proposed 6-week calendar in the SOW: week 0 onboarding + network, week 1 adapter + smoke, week 2 bench runs short context, week 3 bench runs long context and quant profiles, week 4 embedding and end-to-end evaluation, week 5 bugfixes + run extra regression, week 6 handoff and decision.
[09:50] Priya: small question — for embeddings, do you recommend batch sizes of 64 or 128 for throughput?
[09:56] Marcus: depends on memory; we'll test both. start with 64 and 128; we'll report token/sec and GPU usage.
[10:06] Ravi: any known gotchas to watch for?
[10:09] Marcus: watch out for tail latencies on long context models and for cache warming — first requests will be slower. also function calling stateful tooling needs deterministic timeouts to avoid dangling requests.
[10:24] Ken: fine. can you give example code for the proxy adapter approach?
[10:28] Marcus: yes, i'll include a minimal node/python snippet in the follow-up that swaps your current OpenAI calls to Redwood endpoints with a thin shim that injects batching headers and manages KV cache usage.
[10:40] Elena: any other questions?
[10:42] Ravi: one more — do you have any reference customers in logistics who ran similar pilots?
[10:46] Elena: we have a couple of references in supply chain/warehousing; i'll check approvals and share names.
[10:52] Priya: great.
[10:54] Ken: ok let's call it. thanks all.

End of meeting.

References mentioned during call: pilot SOW template (link will be shared), benchmark harness (github gist link to be shared by Marcus), security pack (SOC2 + KMS integration checklist).
